cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a wooden box sanza (thumb piano) with cane tongues, beaded fastening, and incised geometric decoration on the resonator — a plausible Bamileke/Grassfields musical instrument, clearly photographed.

physical.title: sansa
physical.summary: Sansa made of wood of rectangular box form with set of fifteen cane tongues. Outer layer of cane has been stripped away at playing ends to reveal smooth surface; three of tongues are stripped throughout length. Tongues held in place by single metal rod bound with cane; string of clear plastic ? beads and string of red glass ? beads are wrapped around metal rod. Tongues are supported by two bridges, one at lower end made of cane and second at playing end made of wood quadrant. Latter attached to sansa by strip of cane which runs underneath sansa and is wrapped around protruding pegs at either end of bridge. Top front edge of sansa surmounted by two carved inverted triangles flanked by two leaf-shaped motifs. Leather strap tied to each of the carved leaf designs. Box resonator made in several pieces, held together with metal nails. Triangular sound hole below tongues. Lumps of resin ? secured underneath ends of seven tongues. Additional lump of same substance on centre top of fifth tongue from right; other tongues show traces of resin. Front lower end of sansa up to sound hole has incised geometric decoration.
